chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the one who performs i'tikaf (secludes himself in the mosque) and has sexual intercourse, so he said: If he does so, then upon him is what is upon the one who performs dhikr al-zhahir (expiation for divorcing by comparison to one's mother's back).

key_terms.الْمُظَاهِرِ: The one who performs zhahir (divorce by comparison)
key_terms.الْمُعْتَكِفِ: The one performing i'tikaf (seclusion in mosque)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for sexual intercourse during i'tikaf?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the expiation for sexual intercourse during i'tikaf is equivalent to that of 'dhikr al-zhahir' (manifest divorce), a ruling derived by analogy from the severe penalty for consuming one's wife's flesh in Surah Al-Baqarah. This establishes a significant legal precedent in Shia fiqh, linking the sanctity of the mosque retreat with the gravity of marital dissolution penalties.
